title: Where The US Is (Still) Exceptional
gist: Over the past four years US equities have shown no sustained outperformance versus European equities on MSCI mid- and large-cap indexes, so broad 'US exceptionalism' is over; but US consumer discretionary and staples stocks keep beating their European peers, which Gavekal reads as evidence that the exceptional part is the US consumer, not the US market.

themes.theme: End of broad US equity exceptionalism

insights.claim: Measured by MSCI mid- and large-cap indexes, US stocks have shown no sustained trend of relative performance against European stocks over the past four years, meaning the broad US equity market is no longer exceptional.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Portfolios built on a structural US-over-Europe equity overweight have had no payoff for four years; the default home-bias trade needs a fresh justification beyond momentum.
insights.quote: Compared with European stocks, US stocks are no longer exceptional. Over the past four years, there has been no sustained trend in the relative performance of the two, as measured by MSCI mid and large-cap indexes

insights.claim: Index-level comparisons of US versus European equities mask sector-level divergence, so the right analytical unit for the exceptionalism debate is the sector, not the national index.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Argues for expressing regional views through sector pairs rather than country ETFs, since aggregate indexes wash out the parts that still carry a persistent edge.

themes.theme: Consumer sectors as the surviving edge

insights.claim: US consumer discretionary and consumer staples stocks have continued to outperform their European counterparts even as the overall US market stopped outperforming.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A long US consumer sectors versus short European consumer sectors pair is the concentrated residue of the US exceptionalism trade.
insights.quote: US consumer discretionary and staples stocks have continued to outperform their European counterparts
insights.locator: drilling down to the sector level

insights.claim: The persistent outperformance of US consumer sectors is interpreted as evidence that US consumers remain exceptionally resilient in their choices and spending patterns, rather than as a market-wide valuation or liquidity effect.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Frames US consumer spending data as the key variable to monitor for whether this last pocket of relative outperformance holds.
insights.quote: This suggests that while the US market in general is no longer exceptional, US consumers remain exceptionally resilient in their choices and spending patterns.

themes.theme: Forward call on the US consumer

insights.claim: US consumers are expected to remain exceptionally resilient in their spending going forward, sustaining the relative edge of US consumer-facing equities.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Keep consumer-linked US exposure even while trimming broad US index overweights; a break in US consumer resilience would remove the last leg of the exceptionalism case.
insights.quote: Looking ahead, they appear likely to remain so.
